questions.q: Why does this project use WAREHOUSE_SIZE = 'XS' for SUPPORT_WH?
options: The actual workload — loading one small CSV a day and running one summary query — is tiny, so compute size should match it
XS is the only size Snowflake allows for a new account
Larger warehouses cannot run COPY INTO
The VP of Support requires the cheapest possible option regardless of workload
questions.explain: Sizing compute to the actual job, not bigger than needed, is the same right-sized-tool reasoning used throughout this capstone.

options: Suspends the warehouse after 60 seconds of inactivity so Driftwood isn't billed for idle compute
Automatically deletes the warehouse after 60 days
Limits each query to 60 seconds of runtime
Suspends the stage, not the warehouse, after 60 seconds
questions.explain: Auto-suspend stops billing for compute sitting idle between the one daily load and the one daily query.

questions.q: What does the raw table RAW_TICKETS hold?
options: One row per ticket, exactly as exported, with no filtering or transformation applied
Only tickets marked Urgent
A pre-aggregated count of tickets by day
Only tickets from the current week
questions.explain: A raw table holds source data exactly as loaded — any grouping or filtering happens later, in the summary query.

questions.q: Why use ON_ERROR = 'ABORT_STATEMENT' on the COPY INTO load, rather than a more lenient error-handling option?
options: A load that fails loudly on a bad row is safer than one that silently loads a partial day's tickets and under-counts them
ABORT_STATEMENT is required by Snowflake for all CSV loads
It makes the load run faster
It automatically fixes malformed rows instead of rejecting them
questions.explain: For a daily number a stakeholder relies on, a loud, investigated failure beats a quiet, wrong one.

questions.q: What is a simple sanity check to run right after a COPY INTO load?
options: A row count against the raw table, compared to roughly how many tickets came in on a typical day
Dropping and recreating the warehouse
Running the final Power BI report
Granting the analyst role immediately
questions.explain: A quick row count is a cheap way to catch an obviously wrong load (far too few or too many rows) before anyone downstream sees a bad number.
